== Main Success Scenario

// Each step has a semantic anchor like [#step-validate-user]
// Extensions reference these anchors, not numbers
// NOTE: Use [#anchor] syntax (inline) NOT [[anchor]] (block) to avoid breaking list numbering

[#step-{unique-id}-1]
1. *{step-1-action}* +
   _Result: {step-1-result}_

[#step-{unique-id}-2]
2. *{step-2-action}* +
   _Result: {step-2-result}_

[#step-{unique-id}-3]
3. *{step-3-action}* +
   _Result: {step-3-result}_

[#step-{unique-id}-4]
4. *{step-4-action}* +
   _Result: {step-4-result}_

[#step-{unique-id}-5]
5. *{step-5-action}* +
   _Result: {step-5-result}_

== Extensions (Alternative Flows)

// Instead of "3a", use the semantic anchor <<step-UC001-3>>
// If you reorder steps, only the anchor definition moves - references stay valid

=== At <<step-{unique-id}-3>>: {extension-1-name}

*Condition:* {extension-1-condition}

*Steps:*
. {extension-1-step-1}
. {extension-1-step-2}
. *Resume:* Return to <<step-{unique-id}-4>> (or <<step-{unique-id}-5>>, or *ENDS*)

=== At <<step-{unique-id}-3>>: {extension-2-name}

*Condition:* {extension-2-condition}

*Steps:*
. {extension-2-step-1}
. {extension-2-step-2}
. *Resume:* Return to <<step-{unique-id}-4>>

== Example: Semantic vs Numeric References

=== BAD (Numeric - breaks when reordered)
----
Main:
1. User enters credentials
2. System validates user      <- becomes step 3
3. System displays dashboard  <- becomes step 4

Extensions:
2a. Invalid credentials       <- MUST update to 3a
3a. Account locked            <- MUST update to 4a
----

=== GOOD (Semantic - survives reordering)
----
Main:
[#step-enter-creds]
1. User enters credentials
[#step-validate-user]
2. System validates user      <- still "step-validate-user"
[#step-display-dashboard]
3. System displays dashboard  <- still "step-display-dashboard"

Extensions:
=== At <<step-validate-user>>: Invalid credentials  <- no change needed
=== At <<step-display-dashboard>>: Account locked   <- no change needed
----
